inputs.declared_question: How does the Dear Elsewhere instrument carry its commitments about preserved arrangements, included media, turn history, portable reading, and a finite ending into software?

sources_checked.title: Builder Note BN-006: Building Dear Elsewhere

source_facts.claim: I-005 defines seven addressed arrivals, preserved earlier arrangements, bounded included media, explicit saving and handoff, portable exports, and no automatic synchronization or publication.
source_facts.locator: What can arrive; Pass the surface; Let seven be an ending; Choose what to carry onward

source_facts.claim: BN-006 documents one shared JavaScript runtime, seven whole-canvas snapshots, bounded included files, chained turn digests, portable archives, and explicit identity, recovery, conflict, and consent limits.
source_facts.locator: One runtime in three places; Seven snapshots; Carry bytes, retain sources; What a commitment commits to; The portable relic and the context view

cartographer.inference: BN-006 is the technical implementation account for I-005. It turns the Instrument's experiential and procedural commitments into an inspectable runtime and archive model while carrying forward explicit trust and recovery limits.
cartographer.uncertainty: The current prototype does not establish reliable shared hosting, authenticated identity, automatic recovery, conflict merging, consent, or a completed interpersonal trial. Its unsigned hashes cannot establish those properties on their own.
cartographer.attribution: All facts are attributed to exact public Cyberdelic OS publications. The private implementation repository named by BN-006 was not opened or inspected during this run.
cartographer.stop_reason: One strong internal relation completed the bounded continuity explicitly deferred on September 7. No additional candidate was needed.
